stem: A nurse on a perinatal quality-improvement team is reviewing racial and ethnic inequities in maternal outcomes. Which proposed approach best addresses factors that can contribute to those inequities?

options.A: Examine quality-of-care processes, barriers to access, social and structural determinants of health, and potential bias when designing interventions.
options.B: Use patient education about individual health behaviors as the primary intervention and leave health-system factors outside the review.
options.C: Treat equal availability of the same written instructions as evidence that patients have equivalent access to high-quality care.
options.D: Exclude transportation, housing, and interpreter needs from the review because they are not clinical causes of maternal complications.

rationale: A is correct. CDC describes maternal-health inequities as multifactorial and identifies differences in quality of care, social determinants of health, access to care, social and structural determinants, stereotyping, and implicit bias as relevant considerations. CDC guidance for obstetric professionals specifically recommends assessing social and structural determinants, facilitating referrals for identified needs, ensuring interpreter access, recognizing stereotyping, and avoiding attribution of patient behavior solely to individual choices. B is incorrect because an equity review should not isolate individual behavior from health-system and structural factors. C is incorrect because identical written information does not establish equivalent access, communication, or quality of care. D is incorrect because CDC explicitly identifies transportation, housing, language access, and other social or structural factors as relevant to maternal health and health-care use.
educational_objective: When addressing inequities in maternal outcomes, evaluate clinical care quality together with access barriers, social and structural determinants of health, and potential bias rather than attributing outcomes primarily to individual patient behavior.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Working Together to Reduce Black Maternal Mortality; Obstetric Professionals — HEAR HER Campaign
source_version_date: Working Together to Reduce Black Maternal Mortality dated April 8, 2024; Obstetric Professionals — HEAR HER Campaign dated May 15, 2024; current pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Working Together to Reduce Black Maternal Mortality — section describing multiple contributors to disparities: variation in quality healthcare, underlying chronic conditions, and social determinants of health; Obstetric Professionals — HEAR HER Campaign, 'Address Health Inequities': inquire about and document social and structural determinants, maximize referrals to social services, provide interpreter access, recognize stereotyping, avoid solely attributing behavior to individual choices, and address implicit biases.
source_claim_supported: Maternal-health inequities can reflect health-care quality, access, social and structural determinants, and bias; clinicians should assess these factors and avoid reducing patient behavior or outcomes to individual choice alone.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, page 7; Related Activity Statements from the 2024 RN Practice Analysis: 'Participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes' and 'Utilize resources to promote quality client care.'
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — equity-focused perinatal quality improvement
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item from a broad attitudinal statement with obviously false distractors into a realistic perinatal quality-improvement decision. The final item tests whether the candidate recognizes the documented combination of care-quality, access, social/structural, and bias-related contributors without implying that any single factor universally explains disparities.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: maternal health equity / perinatal quality improvement / Management of Care
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current CDC maternal-health and HEAR HER guidance. CDC explicitly identifies quality-of-care variation and social determinants among contributors to maternal-health disparities, and its obstetric-professional guidance addresses social/structural determinants, interpreter access, stereotyping, individual-choice attribution, and implicit bias.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A uses only categories directly supported by CDC and does not claim that any one factor is causal in every case. B conflicts with CDC's explicit warning against attributing behavior solely to individual choices. C incorrectly equates availability of written material with equitable access and quality. D excludes social and language-access factors that CDC specifically directs clinicians to assess or address.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; integrates care-process, access, social/structural, and bias-related domains supported by CDC.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect but plausible; patient education may be useful, but isolating behavior while excluding health-system factors is inconsistent with CDC equity guidance.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect but plausible; standardized written information alone does not demonstrate equitable access, communication, or high-quality care.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect but plausible; transportation, housing, and interpreter needs can materially influence health and use of health care and are relevant to equity-focused review.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A addresses the multifactorial contributors recognized in CDC guidance. B, C, and D each omit or negate a source-supported domain central to the construct.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are framed as proposed quality-improvement approaches and are similar in scope; no choice is made correct by length, grammar, or a unique technical term.
audit_findings.blueprint: The scenario is a nurse participating in a perinatal quality-improvement review, directly mapping to Management of Care performance-improvement and quality-care activity statements in the 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked the final stem and all four options against CDC maternal-health equity and HEAR HER guidance and challenged whether patient education, standardized written information, or exclusion of nonclinical factors could be defensible alternatives. Each failed because CDC explicitly treats social/structural conditions, access, communication, quality, and bias as relevant. No unsupported universal causal claim or second answer remained.
